problem:
Find the general solution to the equation 

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}+3y=-{t}^{4},\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}+3y=0.
$$

Let $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}-3t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+3{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }-3\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+3{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda +3] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-3\lambda +3 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda +3 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =1$ and $\lambda =3.$ Thus, the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}t+{c}_{2}{t}^{3}.
$$

The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is proportional to ${t}^{4}.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form 

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha {t}^{4}
$$

where $\alpha $ is the constant that is to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}t}=4\alpha {t}^{3},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{t}^{2}}=12\alpha {t}^{2}.
$$

To find the value of $\alpha ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}(12\alpha {t}^{2})-3t(4\alpha {t}^{3})+3(\alpha {t}^{4}) & =-{t}^{4} \\ (12\alpha -12\alpha +3\alpha ){t}^{4} & =-{t}^{4} \\ 3\alpha {t}^{4} & =-{t}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get $\alpha =-\frac{1}{3}.$

Hence, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(t)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-\frac{{t}^{4}}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & ={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}t+{c}_{2}{t}^{3}-\frac{{t}^{4}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
